epicondylite.name: Lateral elbow tendinopathy
epicondylite.whatYouFeel: Pain on the outer side of the elbow when gripping, carrying something palm down, or turning a door handle.
epicondylite.whatHappens: The tendons that lift the wrist attach together on the bony bump on the outside of the elbow. This attachment becomes painful when it is overloaded. It usually heals within 6 to 12 months. A cortisone injection relieves quickly but makes relapses more likely.
epicondylite.whoIsAffected: Between 35 and 55, repeated gripping and screwing movements, racket sports.
epicondylite.warning: Swollen or locked elbow, or pins and needles in the hand: see a doctor.

epitro.name: Medial epicondylitis
epitro.whatYouFeel: Pain on the inner side of the elbow when gripping, bending the wrist, or turning the palm down.
epitro.whatHappens: The tendons that bend the wrist and turn the forearm attach on the bony bump on the inside of the elbow.
epitro.whoIsAffected: Golfers, throwers, DIY enthusiasts, manual jobs.
epitro.warning: Pins and needles in the last two fingers as well: see a doctor, the nearby nerve may be affected.

bursite.name: Olecranon bursitis
bursite.commonName: Lump on the point of the elbow
bursite.whatYouFeel: Soft swelling, sometimes the size of an egg, on the point of the elbow, not very painful except when leaning on it.
bursite.whatHappens: A bursa slides between the skin and the point of the elbow. Leaning on it or a knock fills it with fluid.
bursite.whoIsAffected: Repeated leaning on the elbow, after a knock, sometimes with gout.
bursite.warning: Red, hot, painful area, a cut or graze on the elbow, or fever: see a doctor the same day, the bursa may be infected. Do not pierce it yourself.

ulnaire.name: Cubital tunnel syndrome
ulnaire.whatYouFeel: Pins and needles in the little finger and half of the ring finger, worse with the elbow bent, sometimes a clumsy hand.
ulnaire.whatHappens: The ulnar nerve runs in a groove behind the bony bump on the inside of the elbow. It is stretched and compressed there when the elbow stays bent.
ulnaire.whoIsAffected: Leaning on the elbow for long periods, elbow bent for a long time on the phone or at night.
ulnaire.warning: Loss of hand strength or wasting of the muscles between the fingers: see a doctor.

arthrose.name: Elbow osteoarthritis
arthrose.whatYouFeel: Stiffness, especially when straightening the elbow fully, pain at the end of the movement, cracking, sometimes locking.
arthrose.whatHappens: The cartilage wears and bone spurs form, which limit the last few degrees of movement.
arthrose.whoIsAffected: Heavy manual workers, former throwing athletes, after a fracture.
arthrose.warning: Repeated locking or pins and needles in the little finger: see a doctor.

bicepsd.name: Distal biceps tendinopathy
bicepsd.commonName: Pain in the crease of the elbow
bicepsd.whatYouFeel: Deep pain in the crease of the elbow when carrying a load with the elbow bent or when screwing.
bicepsd.whatHappens: The biceps tendon dives into the crease of the elbow to attach on the radius. It bends the elbow and turns the palm up.
bicepsd.whoIsAffected: Men aged 40 to 60, carrying loads, weight training.
bicepsd.warning: A sudden snap in the crease of the elbow with bruising and a lump moving up the arm: see a doctor without delay, within the week. Repair works best in the first two to three weeks.

triceps.name: Triceps tendinopathy
triceps.commonName: Pain at the back of the elbow
triceps.whatYouFeel: Pain just above the point of the elbow when pushing, doing push-ups or dips.
triceps.whatHappens: The triceps tendon attaches on the point of the elbow and straightens the arm.
triceps.whoIsAffected: Weight training, throwing, combat sports, pushing work.
triceps.warning: Unable to straighten the elbow against resistance after a violent effort: see a doctor.

lcu.name: Ulnar (medial) collateral ligament injury
lcu.whatYouFeel: Pain on the inner side of the elbow when throwing, loss of speed and accuracy.
lcu.whatHappens: This ligament holds the elbow when the forearm is pushed outwards, as when cocking the arm to throw. Repeated throwing stretches it.
lcu.whoIsAffected: Throwers: baseball, javelin, handball. In a child who throws, pain in the same place often involves the growth cartilage.
lcu.warning: A snap with sharp pain while throwing: see a doctor. In a child or teenager who throws, any pain on the inner side of the elbow means stopping throwing and getting advice.

radial.name: Radial tunnel syndrome
radial.commonName: Pain on top of the forearm
radial.whatYouFeel: Dull pain a few centimetres below the elbow, on top of the forearm, often mistaken for tennis elbow.
radial.whatHappens: The deep branch of the radial nerve passes through the supinator muscle, where it can be compressed.
radial.warning: Difficulty lifting the fingers or the wrist: see a doctor.

pronateur.name: Pronator teres syndrome
pronateur.commonName: Forearm pain with pins and needles
pronateur.whatYouFeel: Pain at the front of the forearm, pins and needles in the first three fingers on effort, without waking at night.
pronateur.whatHappens: The median nerve passes between the two heads of the pronator teres, just below the crease of the elbow.
pronateur.whoIsAffected: Repeated gripping and palm-down turning movements, weight training.
pronateur.warning: Loss of strength in the thumb–index pinch: see a doctor.

conflit.name: Posterior elbow impingement
conflit.whatYouFeel: Pain at the back of the elbow when it straightens fully, loss of the last few degrees of extension.
conflit.whatHappens: The point of the elbow jams into its hollow at the back of the humerus. Bone spurs can form there.
conflit.whoIsAffected: Throwers, boxers, gymnasts, sports with forceful extension.

ocd.name: Osteochondritis dissecans of the capitellum
ocd.whatYouFeel: Pain on the outer side of the elbow on effort, stiffness, sometimes locking.
ocd.whatHappens: A fragment of bone and cartilage weakens on the capitellum, the part of the humerus that faces the radius.
ocd.whoIsAffected: Children and teenagers aged 10 to 16, especially gymnasts and throwers.
ocd.warning: In a child or teenage athlete, elbow pain lasting more than two weeks, locking, or an elbow that no longer straightens fully: see a doctor and stop throwing and weight-bearing on the hands (cartwheels, handstands, floor work) until then. Carrying on can detach the fragment.

isoext.name: Wrist extension hold
isoext.how: Forearm resting, wrist lifted against a light weight. Hold 30 to 45 s, 5 times.
isoext.videoSearch: tennis elbow isometric wrist extension exercise

excext.name: Slow wrist lowering, palm down
excext.how: Lift with help from the other hand, lower over 4 s. 3 sets of 12.
excext.videoSearch: tennis elbow eccentric wrist extensor exercise

etext.name: Extensor stretch
etext.how: Elbow straight, bend the wrist down with the other hand. 3 times 30 s.

isoflech.name: Wrist flexion hold
isoflech.how: Forearm resting palm up, hold a light weight. Hold 30 to 45 s, 5 times.
isoflech.videoSearch: golfer's elbow isometric wrist flexor exercise

excflech.name: Slow wrist lowering, palm up
excflech.how: Lift with help from the other hand, lower over 4 s. 3 sets of 12.
excflech.videoSearch: golfer's elbow eccentric wrist flexor exercise

etflech.name: Flexor stretch
etflech.how: Elbow straight, palm up, pull the fingers down. 3 times 30 s.

prosup.name: Forearm rotation with a hammer
prosup.how: Elbow at your side, slowly turn the palm up then down. 3 sets of 10.

glace.name: Protect and relieve
glace.how: Avoid leaning on the elbow, use a pad if needed, ice for 15 minutes twice a day.

mob.name: Elbow bending and straightening
mob.how: Bend and straighten the elbow without forcing. 15 times, 3 times a day.

nulnaire.name: Ulnar nerve glide
nulnaire.how: Arm out to the side, palm towards the ceiling. Bend the elbow bringing the hand towards the ear while tilting the head the other way, then come back. 5 slow repetitions, with no lasting pins and needles.

nradial.name: Radial nerve glide
nradial.how: Arm by your side, elbow straight, palm facing back. Bend the wrist down while tilting the head to the same side, then release both at the same time. 5 slow repetitions, with no pins and needles.

nmedian.name: Median nerve glide
nmedian.how: Arm out to the side, palm up, extend then relax the wrist. 5 slow repetitions.

nuit.name: Elbow only slightly bent at night
nuit.how: Avoid sleeping with the elbow fully bent; a towel wrapped around the elbow helps.

curl.name: Elbow curl, slow lowering
curl.how: Light weight, lift in 2 s, lower in 4 s. 3 sets of 10.
curl.videoSearch: eccentric biceps curl distal biceps tendinopathy

triex.name: Elbow extension with a band
triex.how: Elbow close to the body, straighten the arm downwards, return slowly. 3 sets of 12.

serrer.name: Squeeze a soft ball
serrer.how: Squeeze for 5 s without pain. 2 sets of 10.

epaule.name: Shoulder strengthening
epaule.how: External rotation with a band, elbow at your side. 3 sets of 12.
